territorial_scope.description: Applies to exports, reexports and in-country transfers of advanced integrated circuits to foreign adversary countries and to entities located in any country whose own or ultimate parent company headquarters is in a foreign adversary country.

evidence.provision: Sec. 2 (inserting Export Control Reform Act of 2018, Sec. 1758A(a)(1)(B))
evidence.quote: to an entity located in any country

summary.short: Bill to add section 1758A to the Export Control Reform Act of 2018, requiring a license for exports, reexports and in-country transfers of advanced integrated circuits to foreign adversary countries or to entities headquartered there, and denying such license applications, from enactment.
summary.long: The bill adds new section 1758A to the Export Control Reform Act of 2018. From the date of enactment, the Secretary must require a license for the export, reexport or in-country transfer of an advanced integrated circuit to a foreign adversary country, or to an entity located in any country if the entity or its ultimate parent company is headquartered in a foreign adversary country, and must deny any application for such a license. Subsection (b) excludes circuits, and products containing them, that are not designed or marketed for data centers. Subsection (c) defines advanced integrated circuit by reference to Export Control Classification Numbers 3A090 or 4A090 or by specified total processing performance, performance density, DRAM bandwidth and interconnect bandwidth thresholds. Beginning 30 months after enactment, the Secretary may modify these technical parameters by Federal Register notice, after a majority vote of the End-User Review Committee and a briefing to specified congressional committees at least 30 days before publication. Foreign adversary country is defined by reference to 10 U.S.C. 4872(f)(2) and includes the Macau and Hong Kong Special Administrative Regions. The bill sets out no penalties.

notes: Target IDs are empty because no registry IDs were supplied for the Export Control Reform Act, title 10 or the Export Administration Regulations. Sec. 1758A(c)(1)(B) and (C) sit inside the definition paragraph but grant the Secretary a technical-parameter update power and a briefing duty; the bill does not define 'Secretary' or 'End-User Review Committee'. The title refers to 'foreign adversaries' while the operative text uses 'foreign adversary country'. Sec. 1758A(a) applies 'on and after the date of the enactment of this section'; no other effective date is stated. The text is the introduced bill, not an enacted or consolidated version.
